chain.note: Both trees follow the paper's route (rank-saving network, two tape procedures, transforms, resampling and chirps, algorithm, recovery, costs). A states the central saving explicitly (S2.0) and derives it for both networks: s_b (S2.5.6), s_c with its deficit (S2.6.4, S2.6.8), the deficits eta_b, eta_c and tau=sigma (S2.6.14), then both recurrences (S2.9.9, S2.12.7) and the margin g_2 (S6.8). B derives s_b and tau for the bit network (S1.3.4, S1.3.5) but its complex branch is a single quoted infer (S2.1) with no s_c, deficit or sigma, although S2.6.3 relies on a<=m^sigma, so B's chain thins exactly where the layer's saving enters.

overall.reason: Neither plan has a major error; B has one minor sign slip. A carries every checklist sub-step of the six discriminating results (B1-B4, L1-L5, P1-P4, R1-R4, M1, M3, M4, S1-S4, with M2 partial), whereas B carries only L3, R1, S5 and partial B4, L5, R4, M3, M4 and S4. On the central chain A derives both rank savings with eta_b, eta_c and tau=sigma, while B's complex network is a bare quote. A is also more complete on the supporting derivations (packed addition, phase frames, guard widths, time table), and B is nowhere ahead.
